record.tranche_reason: Tests model-wise double descent with a different architecture and an M-sweep in globally gated deep linear networks.
record.gate_note: The study reports generalization error as gating count M varies and describes its behavior around network capacity. Training-error and bias/variance component results are not separate rows because the claim versions name test/generalization error.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps the number of gating units M, which sets model capacity, in globally gated deep linear networks. It reports generalization error diverging at the interpolation threshold and calls the curve double descent. Evidence comes from GP-limit theory, finite-width theory and gradient-descent simulations. This is a different method aimed at the model-wise question (V1). The authors present it as a side result similar to earlier work.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right, but the emphasis is off. The main conclusion is that finite-width GGDLN predictor statistics are governed by kernel shape renormalization, which gives rich dependence on width, depth and regularization and qualitatively matches GD. Double descent with M at network capacity is a side result that the authors note resembles prior linear and nonlinear network findings.
record.recipe_differences: Uses globally gated deep linear networks and varies the number of gating units M; analyzes Bayesian generalization and compares theory with gradient-descent simulations.
record.problems: The double-descent results are presented in figures without numerical values in the text. The finite-width theory is described for a thermodynamic limit with M and L finite, and its agreement with gradient descent is qualitative; the architecture is a specialized GGDLN rather than a standard deep network.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were left out. Training-error and bias/variance component plots in Figure 1 and Supplementary Information Appendix B.1 were not added as separate rows because the versions here concern test/generalization error.

untested.parts: Model size is varied only through gating count M in GGDLNs. There is no width or parameter-count sweep of standard deep nets, and no peak located by training-error criteria in trained conv or transformer models.
No sweep over training epochs; the theory is equilibrium-only.
No sweep of sample count P near the threshold.
Only one model family is studied.
There is no effective-complexity measure predicting the peak across axes, beyond the exact capacity formula for this architecture.
Label noise is fixed (eps=0.1). The peak's dependence on noise and the effect of tuned regularization on the peak are not tested.

missing.what: Error rate keeps falling with M well past capacity (M up to 100), approaching a ReLU network; the authors say over-parameterization does not cause over-fitting here. Theory and GD agree. This bears on the second-descent regime.

record.verdict_notes: There is a minor textual inconsistency: the main text says the variance contribution 'shrinks to 0' at capacity, while the figure captions say it becomes nonzero. The theory uses the T->0 Bayesian posterior with a Gaussian prior, and GD is run without L2. The architecture is specialized: fixed gates and a learned linear path.

versions.untested_parts: Tests varying gating count M in GGDLNs, not ordinary parameter-count or hidden-width scaling in standard deep networks.
No sweep of test error over training epochs.
No sweep of training-sample count near the interpolation threshold.
Does not compare double descent across multiple model classes.
Does not test a single effective-complexity measure predicting peak location across size, epochs, and sample count.
Does not test whether label noise drives the peak, whether multiple peaks occur, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
Does not test whether recasting complexity in effective-parameter terms turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shape.
